كَلِيبٌ : see كَلْبٌ and كَلِبٌ. ―
-b2- Respecting this word in the following verse of TaäbbataSharran, “إِذَا الحَرْبُ أَوْلَتْكَ الكَلِيبَ فَوَلِّهَا
كَلِيبَكَ وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّهَا سَوْفَ تَنْجَلِى
” [When war sets over thee &c.] there are two opinions: one, that by كليب is meant مُكَالِب (see 2): the other, that it is an inf. n. of كَلِبَتِ الحَرْبُ [“ The war became vehement, severe, or fierce ”]: the former is the more valid. (IM.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
